response: Yes, a patient's self-reported health-related quality of life is a prognostic factor for survival in non-small-cell lung cancer patients. Studies have shown that patients who report better health-related quality of life tend to have improved survival rates compared to those with poorer self-reported health-related quality of life. This suggests that health-related quality of life can be a valuable prognostic indicator in non-small-cell lung cancer, in addition to traditional clinical and pathological factors.
